newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay says Taiwan cargo revenue up 8pct.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says Taiwan cargo revenue up 8pct.

text.p: Cargo revenue for Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd in Taiwan has increased by 8 per cent this year compared to 1995, according to the airline's in-house newspaper.
It said total tonnage for all airlines ex-Taiwan in 1996 is expected to reach 429,112 tonnes, compared to 404,785 tonnes in 1995.
Total tonnage on Cathay aircraft leaving Taipei's Chiang Kai-shek (CSK) airport was 53,160 tonnes this year compared with 48,447 in 1995,a 9.7 per cent rise.

Cathay's share of the local air cargo market rose to 12.39 percent from from 11.97 to 12.39 per cent, it added. Cathay is the largest foreign carrier in Taiwan and the second largest passenger carrier from CSK, according to the airline.
Cathay said the increase in cargo revenue was helped by new services to Toronto, New York and Chicago "which opened up a whole new market."

"The increase is particularly sweet as Taiwan has to overcome obstacles such as all Cathay cargo exported from Taipei, except to Tokyo and Seoul, has to be shipped via Hong Kong because of cargo traffic rights," the newspaper said.
"These constraints do not make life easy for the Cathay cargo team in Taiwan. We face the threat of offloading constantly," cargo manager Clint Chu was quoted as saying.
Tuna, eels,electronics, computer products, spare parts, shoe material and garments are the main items carried Chu said.

He added Cathay will focus on yield in 1997 as Taiwan is a low yield market and Cathay already has a strategy in place to keep on expanding by widening distribution, incorporating more agents and intensifying business relationships.

Industry sources said Cathay has faced more competition in the highly competitive market as Taiwanese carrier EVA Air began three times daily flights in August using Boeing 747 Combi aircraft. Cathay also handed over its three times daily Kaohsiung service to Dragonair as part of a new air agreement.

Cathay currently flies 100 passenger flights a week from Hong Kong to Taipei as well as six freighter flights a week which continue onto Tokyo Narita, an airline spokeswoman said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
